key_insight: ConSDL discovers more reproducible concepts by replacing a sparse autoencoder’s linear encoder with per-sample sparse coding.
engineering_relevance: More consistent dictionaries and coefficients across training seeds can improve the reliability of foundation-model interpretability analyses.
method: Replace the standard linear encoder with per-sample sparse optimization.
Learn dictionaries using the optimized sparse coefficients.
Evaluate recovery on synthetic data and cross-seed consistency in vision and language settings.
evidence_signal: ConSDL achieves near-perfect dictionary and coefficient recovery across 16 synthetic settings and improves their cross-seed consistency by 17.6% and 35.9%, respectively, over the average of six SAE baselines across four vision and language settings.
watch_item: Per-sample optimization may increase computational cost relative to a single encoder pass; the abstract does not quantify this trade-off.
paper_title: Beyond SAEs: Consistent Concept Discovery with Sparse Coding
